newsitem.title: USA: IMM currencies end down before Saturday EU meeting.
newsitem.headline: IMM currencies end down before Saturday EU meeting.

text.p: IMM currency futures settled lower ahead of an European Union (EU) meeting on Saturday to discuss Italy's formal request to return the lira to the European exchange rate mechanism (ERM), traders and analysts said.
December marks weakened throughout the day, as cash marks gave up ground against the Italian lira, fell off a two-month high of 3.3975 against the French franc and weakened against the yen.
Cash mark weakness provided limited momentum for the dollar, as the U.S. currency could not rise to 1.51 spot.
As a result, December marks held losses slightly above the 1.51-spot equivalent of $0.6631.
One French-based firm bought 8,000 February 6450 mark puts late in the day, as the market focused on the implications of the lira's return to the ERM.
Another firm reportedly bought 5,000 February 87 yen puts late in the day.
Michael Faust, a currency analyst at Bailard, Biehl & Kaiser, said weakness in the dollar/yen could provide leadership to the dollar, which has been overshadowed by the activity in the cash crosses.
"With the tankan out of Japan next week, that may allow people to form stronger opinions about Japanese interest rates and economic growth," Faust said.
Japan's "tankan" or business sentiment survey will be released on Wednesday, November 27.

December sterling corrected gains, falling through support at $1.6760, while Australian dollars held support at the overnight low of $0.8080. Some traders said December Australian dollars could slip to $0.8050 in the near term.

At the end of pit trade, December yen was off $0.000018 at $0.008993, marks were off $0.0042 at $0.6644, Swiss francs were $0.0026 lower at $0.7889, sterling fell $0.0098 at $1.6788, Canadian dollars were down $0.0014 at $0.7467, Australian dollars were up $0.0018 at $0.8136 and Mexican pesos were down $0.000175 at $0.124825.
